items.title: A finite stably free module modulo an ideal in the Jacobson radical lifts to a finite stably free module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra), section Stably free modules
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts a finite stably free module E over R/I to a finite stably free module over R itself when I lies in the Jacobson radical (statement lines 94-97). The proof first replaces E by an explicit isomorphism E + (R/I)^n = (R/I)^m, then has to choose two R-linear lifts phi and psi of the corresponding projection and injection (proof lines 101-106), and to prove that the composite phi o psi, which is only congruent to the identity modulo I, is actually invertible: this is done by inspecting its determinant, which lies in 1 + I and is therefore a unit by the hypothesis on I (proof lines 107-109). The last step reads the kernel of the split surjection phi off as a direct summand of a finite free module, hence stably free, and checks that it reduces to E (proof lines 110-111). The non-routine ingredient is the determinant argument, which upgrades a congruence modulo I to genuine invertibility without any locality or Nakayama input; nothing beyond the two reductions is cited.
